The point of junction between two things, in particular a support, that abuts.
The solid portion of a structure that supports the lateral pressure of an arch or vault.
A construction that supports the ends of a bridge; a structure that anchors the cables on a suspension bridge.

examples.text: Each of the bridges consists of six separate girder spans on brick abutments.

glosses: The part of a valley or canyon wall against which a dam is constructed.

examples.text: Heavy rains have caused the dam's abutments to seep, raising concern over possible dam failure.

glosses: Something that abuts, or on which something abuts.
The state of abutting.
That element that shares a common boundary or surface with its neighbor.
The tooth that supports a denture or bridge.
A fixed point or surface where resistance is obtained.

examples.text: The fulcrum acted as an abutment.

glosses: An object placed against or under another, to support it; anything that supports.

examples.text: They stuck a block of wood under it as a prop.

glosses: The player on either side of the hooker in a scrum.
Any of the seashells in the game of props.
To support or shore up something.

examples.text: Try using a phone book to prop up the table where the foot is missing.

glosses: To play rugby in the prop position.
To position the feet of (a person) while sitting, lying down, or reclining so that the knees are elevated at a higher level.

To stop suddenly or unexpectedly; derived from the situation where a horse might suddenly halt of its own accord, digging its front hooves into the ground to brace itself from forward movement, potentially unseating its rider.
To knock (a person) down.

examples.text: We used to go out into the roads (highway robbery) between races, and if we met an ‘old bloke’ (man) we ‘propped him’ (knocked him down), and robbed him.

glosses: An item placed on a stage or set to create a scene or scenario in which actors perform.

examples.text: They used the trophy as a prop in the movie.

glosses: An item placed within an advertisement in order to suggest a style of living etc.

examples.text: You can use props in a literal way to enhance the story, such as shooting a woodworker amidst woodworking tools.

glosses: The propeller of an aircraft or boat.
To manually start the engine of a propeller-driven aircraft with no electric starter by pulling vigorously on one of the propeller blades using the hands, so that the propeller can catch ignition.

examples.text: There was some good counter hits, and then Foster received a prop on the nose which drew the claret.

Ce qui sert à soutenir une chose ou une personne pour l’empêcher de tomber, de chanceler, etc.

examples.text: Une grande terrasse dallée, entourée d’un mur à hauteur d’appui, s’étendait devant la porte d’entrée.
Mettre un appui, des appuis à un mur. Cette muraille a besoin d’appui. Si on ne donne un appui à cet arbre, le vent l’abattra.

glosses: Ce sur quoi on s’appuie.

examples.text: L’appui de cette croisée est dangereux, il est trop bas. Tablette d’appui. Barre d'appui.

glosses: La partie d’une fenêtre, d’une balustrade, etc., sur laquelle on peut s’appuyer.

examples.text: L'ensemble du linteau, de deux poteaux d’huisserie et de l’appui E, constitue l’huisserie d'une porte ou d'une fenêtre.
Capestang, en parlant ainsi, enjambait l'appui de la fenêtre.
La dame s’accoudait maintenant à la fenêtre, étalant ses bouteilles sur la pierre d’appui.

examples.text: Ce cheval a l’appui bon.

glosses: Temps pendant lequel, dans la marche, le pied du cheval pose sur le sol.

examples.text: Note : Que l’on nomme autrement foulée.

glosses: Élévation plus ou moins sensible de la voix dans le phrasé.

examples.text: L’accent tonique marque un appui de la voix sur la voyelle qui le porte.

glosses: Aide ; protection.

examples.text: Euphrasie. Je conçois parfaitement... en votre qualité d'avocat de M. le comte, vous cherchez à m'effrayer... vous voudriez que nous nous privassions nous-mêmes de l’appui d'une personne qui nous est dévouée.
